Arabah
AR-uh-buh
proper noun
Hebrew arabah, “plain, desert, dry place”; the great rift-valley of the Jordan running from the sea of Chinnereth down to the salt sea; the KJV renders it “the plain” and “the champaign.”

📖 Biblical Definition

The Arabah is the great cleft in the earth through which the Jordan runs, the deepest depression on the face of the ground, sinking from the waters of Chinnereth down to the salt sea, the lowest dry land under heaven. The KJV nameth it the plain and the champaign: Moses spake unto all Israel on this side Jordan in the wilderness, in the plain over against the Red sea (Deu 1:1), and the plain, from Chinnereth even unto the sea of the plain, even the salt sea, was reckoned to Israel (Deu 3:17). Through this low place the pilgrim people passed toward the promise, and its very depth is a parable. The way to Canaan led downward before it led up; the road to the inheritance ran through the deepest valley of all. So the Christian’s path to glory descendeth through humbling and death before it riseth. And at the bottom of the Arabah lieth the salt sea, that dead and bitter water covering the plain where Sodom stood, a standing witness to the judgment of God upon sin. The pilgrim walketh beside it and remembereth: here fire came down from heaven; here the cities of the plain became an ensample, set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire. The Arabah thus holdeth both the low road of the humble and the memorial of wrath, and bids the traveller press through the valley toward the city that hath foundations.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The great rift-valley of the Jordan, the lowest dry land on earth, running down to the salt sea; KJV “the plain,” “the champaign” (Deu 1:1; 3:17); a parable of the low road to the promise and a memorial of judgment on Sodom.

ARABAH, the great rift-valley of the Jordan, rendered in the KJV “the plain” and “the champaign.”

It runs from the sea of Chinnereth down to the salt sea (Deu 3:17).

The deepest depression of the earth, the lowest dry land under heaven.

The pilgrim host passed through it toward the promised land (Deu 1:1).

At its floor lies the salt sea, witness to the judgment upon Sodom.

📖 Key Scripture

Deu 1:1 — "These be the words which Moses spake unto all Israel on this side Jordan in the wilderness, in the plain over against the Red sea, between Paran, and Tophel, and Laban, and Hazeroth, and Dizahab."

Deu 11:30 — "Are they not on the other side Jordan, by the way where the sun goeth down, in the land of the Canaanites, which dwell in the champaign over against Gilgal, beside the plains of Moreh?"

Heb 13:14 — "For here have we no continuing city, but we seek one to come."

1Pe 2:11 — "Dearly beloved, I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul;"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

No live redefinition attends this valley; the truth to recover is that the road to the promise runs through the low place, and the salt sea abides as a witness to God’s judgment on sin.

expand to see more

The Arabah is a plain geographical reality, the Jordan rift and the salt sea basin still measurable as the lowest land on earth.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is twofold. The pilgrim way to the inheritance leadeth downward through humbling before it leadeth up to glory, as the believer must be brought low that he may be exalted in due time. And the salt sea remaineth a solemn memorial that God did not spare the cities of the plain, but made them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly. The low road and the dead sea preach humility and holy fear together.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Arabah means a plain, desert, or dry sterile place; it names the Jordan rift and, in the plural, the plains of Moab and of Jericho.

expand to see more

Arabah — Hebrew arabah, a plain, desert, or dry sterile place.

Rendered in the KJV as “the plain,” “the champaign,” and “the desert.”

The plural araboth gives the plains of Moab and the plains of Jericho.

The root conveys aridity and sterility, a waste untilled land.

The sea of the plain is the salt sea, at the valley’s lowest floor.

Usage

"Moses spake to Israel in the plain, that is, the Arabah, beyond Jordan."

"The Arabah runs down to the salt sea, the sea of the plain."

"The pilgrim passes through the Arabah, the low road to the promise."
